current.rappels: Rappel the Ellen Pea line: 4 rappels on two 60 m ropes (about 15, 55, 50 and 40 m), or walk off to the west
current.rappel_count_note: This route descends Ellen Pea’s rappel line. Four rappels on two 60 m ropes: every rappel needs both ropes. Nearly every anchor is bolted below the top trees, and some rappels are diagonal, so steer to stay on line. About an hour from the top to the base. Instead of rappelling, you can traverse off to a 3rd-class ramp partway down.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 4, about 15 m, trending slightly left to a larger tree.
rappel_detail.station: The slung tree at the top of the route.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 4, about 55 m, into the left side of the right-hand cave. Then walk right to the bolted anchor above pitch 2.
rappel_detail.station: The larger tree below and left of the top.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 3 of 4, about 50 m, down and right.
hazards: Diagonal: you have to steer to stay on line for the next anchor.
rappel_detail.station: The bolted anchor above pitch 2, reached by walking right in the cave.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 4 of 4, about 40 m, to the narrow ledge at the base.
rappel_detail.station: The next bolted anchor down and right.

current.descent_text: From the top, rappel down the Ellen Pea line using two ropes (diagonal rappelling is required in places), or walk down via the 3rd-class terrain to the west.

current.rappels: 7 rappels on two 70 m ropes down the route; or scramble off down and left on a treed ramp into the 3rd-class gully, or rappel the Ellen Pea line
current.rappel_count_note: Seven rappels on two 70 m ropes, one of them a rope-stretching 61 m from the cave. A non-rappel descent tops out and scrambles down and left on a treed ramp into the 3rd-class gully left of the wall. From the base, walk left down the gully, or rappel the bolted slab below and right: about 75 m more, on three bolted anchors.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 7, about 35 m on two 70 m ropes, angling left to the ledge atop pitch 10.
rappel_detail.station: From an anchor on the right edge of the highest summit overhangs.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 7, about 30 m on two 70 m ropes, down the flake pitch.
rappel_detail.station: From the ledge atop pitch 10.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 3 of 7, about 40 m on two 70 m ropes, angling hard right; fixed wires are in place for directionals on the strand you will not pull.
rappel_detail.station: From the anchor below the flake pitch.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 4 of 7, about 45 m on two 70 m ropes, into the cave.
rappel_detail.station: From the next anchor.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 5 of 7, about 61 m on two 70 m ropes, a rope-stretching rappel to the ledge atop pitch 3.
hazards: This one stretches two 70 m ropes; knot the ends.
rappel_detail.station: From the cave.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 6 of 7, about 45 m on two 70 m ropes, down pitch 3.
rappel_detail.station: From the ledge atop pitch 3.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 7 of 7, about 60 m on two 70 m ropes, down and slightly right over the terrain of pitches 1 and 2.
rappel_detail.station: From the anchor at the foot of pitch 3.

current.descent_text: Descend via double-rope rappels down the line of The Tiger using 70m ropes; alternatively, traverse across to the Ellen Pea route line for a rappel descent, or walk off via the 3rd-class ledge system to the west/summit ridge.

current.rappels: 2-3 raps (two 30 m ropes) from the upper gully/East Ridge down to roughly the saddle above Lake Serene; anchors are typically slung trees, horns, or pickets rather than fixed hardware.

rappel_detail.notes: First of two 30m rappels used to descend the steep, forested upper East Ridge section in winter conditions.
Second 30m rappel continuing down the forested East Ridge before downclimbing or boot-skiing the Hourglass Gully itself.

current.descent_text: The descent mirrors the ascent route but is significantly more technical. On the upper East Ridge, climbers set up two 30-meter rappels using existing rap slings in trees. Descending the Hourglass Gully in spring conditions often involves boot-skiing down 40-50 degree slopes with small wet slides. The steep constriction requires careful down-climbing or short rappels. The ridge traverse back to the lake saddle is exposed with 1,000-foot drops to the northeast side. Return to Lake Serene via the approach slope and descend the 4.1-mile trail by headlamp if a very early start was not made.

current.rappels: 2 double-rope rappels: one from near the summit to the notch between Middle and South Gunsight, one more into the moat at the base of the notch. With only one 60 m rope expect roughly twice as many; no single-rope count is published.
current.rappel_count_note: A first-hand report of the East Face 5.10d describes one double-rope rappel to the notch between Middle and South Gunsight, then one more — loose, dirty and cold — into the moat at the base of the notch. The figure of about four rappels on a single 60 m rope is arithmetic from roughly 100 m of descent rather than a published count.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 2, double-rope, to the notch between Middle and South Gunsight.
rappel_detail.anchor: south-facing rappel anchor near the summit
rappel_detail.station: Traverse south along the summit ridge from the top to the south-facing rappel anchors.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 2, double-rope, into the moat at the base of the notch.
rappel_detail.anchor: anchor at the Middle-South Gunsight notch
hazards: Loose, dirty and cold. Then navigate the crevasse field on the Chickamin Glacier back to camp.
rappel_detail.station: The notch between Middle and South Gunsight.

current.descent_text: After summiting, traverse south along the summit ridge to the south-facing rappel anchors. Make one double-rope rappel to the notch between Middle and South Gunsight, then a second, loose and dirty one into the moat at the base of the notch. Navigate the crevasse field on Chickamin Glacier to return to base camp.

current.rappels: 2 double-rope (2x60 m) rappels down the West Face, separated by belayed downclimbing of the summit ridge and several hundred feet of Class 3 on the dike
current.rappel_count_note: A four-station sequence of 50/50/50/20 m is sometimes attached to this route. It matches, figure for figure, the descent of north Gunsight Peak's West Face — a 5.11+, 6-pitch, 600 ft rock route on a different summit — and does not belong to this Class 5.6 glacier route on the main spire. Nothing about those figures was measured here, so they are not carried. What is documented for this route is two double-rope rappels: after belaying back down the exposed summit ridge, one double-rope rappel down the west face, then a diagonal double-rope rappel, with directional protection placed along the way, that reaches the snow finger in one go. That descent used two 60 m ropes. No single-rope descent of this route is documented.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 2, double-rope (two 60 m ropes), down the West Face to the base of the black basalt dike. Then scramble several hundred feet of Class 3 down the dike to the top of the crux dihedral.
rappel_detail.anchor: large horn thickly slung with rappel webbing, about 50 ft below the true summit
rappel_detail.station: Belay and downclimb the exposed summit ridge back to the large slung horn about 50 ft below the top, a good confirmation that you are on the descent.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 2, a diagonal double-rope rappel that reaches the snow finger in one go.
rappel_detail.anchor: natural anchor (slung horn, block or chockstone) at the top of the crux dihedral
hazards: The last person down should place a directional piece so the rope runs true on the diagonal.
rappel_detail.station: The top of the crux dihedral, reached by scrambling down the dike.

current.descent_text: Reverse the ridge crest from the summit: belay/downclimb the exposed summit ridge back down to a large horn about 50' below the true summit that is thickly slung with rappel webbing (a good on-route confirmation marker). From there, make a double-rope (60m x 2) rappel down the West Face to regain the base of the route's black basaltic dike/dihedral. Scramble down several hundred feet of Class 3 terrain on the dike to the top of the crux dihedral, then make a second, diagonal double-rope (60m x 2) rappel — the last person down should place a directional piece of protection to keep the rope running true — which in one pull reaches the snow finger below. From the snow finger, downclimb or glissade back onto the Chikamin Glacier and reverse the approach (re-climb to the Chikamin-Dome col, cross the Dome Glacier, over Itswoot Pass/Cub Pass, down Bachelor Meadows/Bachelor Creek, and out Downey Creek Trail #768) to the trailhead. All anchors reported on this route are natural — slung horns, blocks, and chockstones — with no fixed/bolted stations, consistent with its remote, low-traffic character. Typical parties use two 60m ropes for both rappels; expect the crux dihedral's black rock to be loose in spots, and factor in real crevasse-travel time and daylight for the long glacier return to camp.

current.rappels: 2 double-rope rappels: one from near the summit to the notch between Middle and South Gunsight, one more into the moat at the base of the notch. With only one 60 m rope expect more; no single-rope count is published.
current.rappel_count_note: A first-hand report of the East Face 5.10d describes one double-rope rappel to the notch between Middle and South Gunsight, then one more — loose, dirty and cold — into the moat at the base of the notch. The figure of about four rappels on a single 60 m rope is arithmetic from roughly 100 m of descent rather than a published count.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 2, double-rope, to the notch between Middle and South Gunsight.
rappel_detail.anchor: south-facing rappel anchor near the summit
rappel_detail.station: Traverse south along the summit ridge from the top to the south-facing rappel anchors.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 2, double-rope, into the moat at the base of the notch.
rappel_detail.anchor: anchor at the Middle-South Gunsight notch
hazards: Loose, dirty and cold. Then navigate the crevasse field on the Chickamin Glacier back to camp.
rappel_detail.station: The notch between Middle and South Gunsight.

current.descent_text: From the summit, traverse south along the summit ridge to the south-facing rappel anchors and make two double-rope rappels: the first to the notch between Middle and South Gunsight, the second into the moat at the base of the notch (loose, dirty and cold). With a single 60 m rope expect more rappels. From the glacier, reverse the approach: descend roughly 5,000 ft back to Agnes Creek and hike out 9-10 miles to High Bridge.

current.rappels: 4 rappels on a single 60 m rope, or three with two ropes; one lower rappel is overhanging
current.rappel_count_note: Counted for one 60 m rope: a rappel from a ledge just below the summit, a single-rope rappel from the bottom of the shoulder to the top of pitch 2, then the overhanging drop to below Gunsight Notch in two rappels. With two ropes, that last drop is one double-rope rappel, so three in all. Anchors are natural slings and cord; parties report adding cord to one and rebuilding another.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 4, down the steepest upper wall to the shoulder.
rappel_detail.anchor: anchor on a small ledge, east side just below the summit
hazards: Rockfall-prone: the next rappeller should move off to the side at the bottom, not straight down, since others may be rappelling above.
rappel_detail.station: A small ledge on the east side, slightly below the summit, reached by downclimbing the final scramble.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 4, a full single 60 m rope doubled, to the belay station at the top of the second climbing pitch.
rappel_detail.anchor: belay/anchor stance at the bottom of the shoulder
hazards: The buttress rock is loose enough that downclimbing this section is not recommended.
rappel_detail.station: The bottom of the shoulder.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 3 of 4: on a single rope, the first half of the overhanging drop, to an intermediate stance. With two ropes, this and the next are one double-rope rappel.
rappel_detail.anchor: belay station at the top of pitch 2 (fixed natural slings)
hazards: The rappel is overhanging. Knot the rope ends.
rappel_detail.station: The belay station at the top of the second climbing pitch, a tree at the top of the drop overlooking the V-notch.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 4 of 4, to just below the north side of Gunsight Notch.
rappel_detail.anchor: intermediate anchor (natural slings or cord; carry cord to rebuild)
hazards: Anchors here have been found needing extra cord or a rebuild.
rappel_detail.station: Intermediate stance partway down the overhanging section.

current.descent_text: Descend by reversing the final scramble pitches/downclimbing back to the top of the technical face (the uppermost section is a downclimb/scramble to the top of the East Face), then begin a rappel sequence rather than trying to downclimb the buttress itself — the rock is loose enough that down-climbing the route is not recommended. From a small ledge/anchor on the east side just below the summit, a 50 m rappel gets you down the steepest upper wall (rockfall-prone — the next rappeller should move off to the side immediately, not straight down, to avoid anyone above). Below that, from the bottom of the shoulder, one rappel on a single 60 m rope reaches the belay station at the top of the second climbing pitch. From there the line drops over an overhanging section to just below the north side of Gunsight Notch: one double-rope rappel with two ropes, or two rappels on a single 60 m rope. That is four rappels on one 60 m rope, which is what parties report, or three with two ropes. Anchors are fixed natural slings and cord rather than bolts, and parties regularly add cord or rebuild one, so carry some. Move off the fall line as soon as you are down each rappel; rockfall knocked loose by the party above is a recognized hazard here. Below the notch, re-descend the glacier and snowfield and Mixup Arm to Cascade Pass.
